title: Cohomology properties of maps in (Cat) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the lemma on the previous page characterizes totally W-aspherical small categories A, the setting of test categories and modelizers as in Pursuing Stacks. Here W is a basic localizer on (Cat). W_A is the class of maps of presheaves F→G in A^ such that A_{/F}→A_{/G} lies in W. Hot_A = (W_A)^{-1}A^, and γ: A^→Hot_A is the localization functor. The four conditions are: (i) A totally W-aspherical; (ii) W_A stable under finite products; (ii bis) f∈W_A ⇒ f×id_Z∈W_A; (iii)/(iv) the functors A^→Hot_A and A^→Hot(W) commute with finite products.

Top of the page: end of the proof that (ii) implies (iii), specifically the injectivity of Hom_{Hot}(X,ΠY_i)→ΠHom_{Hot}(X,Y_i).
- Take f,g: X⇉Y' with Y→Y' (α∈W).
- For each factor, the hypothesis gives β_i∈W and φ_i with β_i p_i = φ_i α and φ_i f ≃ φ_i g.
- Set β=Πβ_i: Y=ΠY_i→Y''=ΠY'_i and φ=(φ_i). Then β∈W by (ii), and the diagram commutes.
- Since φf∼φg, we get γ(f)=γ(g).
NB: the same argument would work for infinite products if W_A were stable under infinite products.

Next he returns to the lemma.
- (ii)⇔(ii bis) is trivial (f×g = (f×id)(id×g)).
- (ii)⇒(iii) has just been proved. The margin says the converse is evident once one knows W_A is strongly saturated.
- (ii bis) is local on Z, so it suffices to take Z=a∈A. In the square X×a→Y×a over X→Y, it then suffices that the projections X×a→X (and Y×a→Y) lie in W_A. This is the condition 'A loc. asph.', i.e. products with representables are aspherical over the base. So (i)⇒(ii bis).
- Conversely, if A is aspherical, apply (ii bis) to f: a→e_{A^}, which lies in W_A since A_{/a} has a final object and A is aspherical. This gives a×b→b∈W_A, i.e. a×b is aspherical.
- Hence (i)⇔(ii)+A aspherical. This corrects the unconditional equivalence written on the previous page.

The next page handles (iv) via A_{/X×Y}→A_{/X}×A_{/Y} being aspherical.
errors: The previous page states (i)⇔(ii) unconditionally. Here Grothendieck himself corrects this to (i)⇔(ii)+A aspherical; (ii) alone does not force A aspherical, e.g. it fails for the empty-type degenerate cases.
The marginal claim that (iii)⇒(ii) is 'évident' relies on strong saturation of W_A (W_A = maps inverted by γ). This is true for basic localizers but is not proved here.
The phrase 'A est loc. asph.' is used loosely for the condition that X×a→X∈W_A for all X. In the standard terminology this is part of total asphericity, not 'local asphericity'.

ideas.what: Characterization of totally aspherical small categories: A aspherical and W_A stable under finite products, equivalently A^→Hot_A or A^→Hot(W) preserves finite products
ideas.modern_name: totally aspherical categories / compatibility of the localization with finite products
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Pursuing Stacks), systematized by Maltsiniotis (Astérisque 301) and Cisinski (Astérisque 308)
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (sections on totally aspherical/test categories)

ideas.what: Localization preserves finite products when the weak equivalences are stable under finite products (proof via the calculus of the diagram β=Πβ_i)
Remark that infinite products would be preserved if W_A were stable under infinite products
ideas.modern_name: stability of weak equivalences under arbitrary products

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful working-out of a lemma on total asphericity that is essentially in Pursuing Stacks and in Maltsiniotis' and Cisinski's expositions. The only point of note is the self-correction that A must be assumed aspherical, which is standard.
transcription_corrections: The margin reads 'est évident quand on sait que W_A est fortement saturé (resp. ... saturé)'. The arrow it annotates is ⇑ from (iii) to (ii), not part of the ⇓ statement.
The marginal note beside 'Z dans A' is 'raisonnement déjà fait plus haut'; this is correctly placed.
The last line reads 'donc (i) ⟺ (ii) + A asphérique'. The (ii) here is the finite-product stability condition.
